name: Tyla
label: FAX / Epic
lede: She heard a log drum at 14, sang over it at 17, and at 21 became the first South African soloist on the Hot 100 in 55 years with a song about a body in motion and a dance that ends with a pour.

eras.title: A log drum in a Johannesburg school
eras.text: Tyla Laura Seethal grew up on Johannesburg's East Rand, found amapiano in a free period, and put her own pop vocals over it while the scene's stars were mostly chanting. That choice became a sound, then a fight about a label for it.

years.h: Born in Edenvale, third of five kids
years.p: Tyla Seethal grew up in Johannesburg and graduated from Edenglen High School in 2019, where she was head of culture.
years.xp:
Wikipedia puts her birth in Edenvale on Gauteng's East Rand, with Indian, Mauritian, Zulu and Irish ancestry. Dazed says it was a traditional household where swearing and on-screen kissing were discouraged, and that she was posting YouTube videos of herself singing [[Justin Bieber|e0140a67-e4d1-4f13-8a01-364355bee46e]] at 11.

At 14 she heard Kwiish SA's "Iskhathi (Gong Gong)" in a school free period and knew the log drum was something. Her own influences run to [[Michael Jackson|f27ec8db-af05-4f36-916e-3d57f91ecf5e]], [[Rihanna|73e5e69d-3554-40d8-8516-00cb38737a1c]] and [[Aaliyah|bc85da58-52d9-457d-ae8d-5d8d4ec870a9]].

years.cap: Tyla hosting the 2025 Kids' Choice Awards · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Getting Late (Tyla song) · Dazed: Tyla interview · Wikipedia: Tyla (singer)
years.h: "Getting Late": a 17-year-old sings over amapiano, unsigned
years.p: Self-released with [[Kooldrink|1b427bbb-62b2-4693-9076-ee92355addb3]] and producer Rogan Kelly, it set a pop hook over a genre where longer tracks mostly ran on chants.
years.xp:
The video only arrived on January 28, 2021, after lockdown filming, directed by her then-manager; Wikipedia says it passed 2 million views by May 2021 and that a TikTok dance she started pulled over 10.8 million likes. It also earned a South African Music Award nomination for Best Music Video.

Tyla has said she wanted to bring pop to a scene she saw as male dominated. Dazed notes the song sparked an argument about whether she belonged in amapiano at all, and that critics started calling the hybrid "popiano".

eras.title: Mining engineering or a record deal
eras.text: She enrolled for mining engineering to keep her parents happy, then talked them into one year for music. A major label got to her first.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tyla (singer) · Dazed: Tyla interview · TheGrio: Tyla profile · Wikipedia: Getting Late (Tyla song)
years.h: Epic signs a 19-year-old on a parental gap year
years.p: Epic Records president Ezekiel Lewis called her "the most precious African export", in Dazed's telling, and signed her through the FAX joint venture.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the signing to May 2021; the Getting Late article says June. Either way the gap year became a career: Dazed lists development sessions with [[will.i.am|d574c9bd-46f6-440a-8d6a-8412a283eeb1]] and [[Tricky Stewart|1d65f4c5-e6a2-48f3-b8ec-1a151ed124b1]] across Dubai, Cape Town, Los Angeles, Miami and Atlanta.

She told Rolling Stone, via TheGrio, that it took "a lot of begging and crying" to get her parents to agree. First release on the deal was "Overdue" in October 2021, with [[DJ Lag|1b6bf4fa-f2af-42c7-8399-53cc2bd468ec]] and Kooldrink.

eras.title: Water
eras.text: A sleeper single, a dance that ends in a pour, and a Hot 100 entry no South African soloist had managed since 1968.

years.cap: Tyla at the WNBA All-Star Game, 25 July 2026 · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Water (Tyla song) · Music Week: Hitmakers, Sammy SoSo · OkayAfrica: Sammy Soso interview · Wikipedia: Amapiano
years.h: "Water": Sammy Soso, a Kelvin Momo sample, four cities
years.p: Built in London, finished in Los Angeles, demoed in Atlanta and recorded for good in Cape Town, it was produced by [[Sammy Soso|44c1e43c-24d4-4995-9d68-acfa0cb14f13]] and lifted a sample from [[Kelvin Momo|c5726285-7b7c-43ce-b107-dae084cf5e6c]].
years.xp:
Music Week's producer interview says Soso started getting "100 missed calls" once it caught fire. Co-writers with Soso include Ari PenSmith, Mocha Bands and Believve, per OkayAfrica.

Kelvin Momo is the figure credited with "Private School Piano", the soulful, live-instrument end of amapiano, which makes him a pointed sample source for a pop record.

yt: Tyla on the dance, Drake and the Grammy
years.h: The dance: a hip roll, then a pour down the back
years.p: South African dancer Lee-ché "Litchi" Janecke choreographed it from the Bacardi style that came up in Pretoria, and "Water" entered the Hot 100 at No. 67.
years.xp:
The challenge took off in August 2023 after Tyla performed the choreography live. By October the two main hashtags had passed 446.8 million views across 600,000-plus videos, per Wikipedia.

The song kept climbing to No. 7 on January 13, 2024. Wikipedia calls her the first South African soloist on the Hot 100 in over 55 years, since [[Hugh Masekela|83a2e0fb-3d9b-46ff-b383-3dde54c15297]]'s "Grazing in the Grass" in 1968. She also opened dates on [[Chris Brown|c234fa42-e6a6-443e-937e-2f4b073538a3]]'s Under the Influence tour in 2023.

years.h: Travis Scott and Marshmello each take a turn
years.p: Two remixes arrived the same day; the Travis Scott version became the 14th track on her album.

eras.title: Tyla, the record
eras.text: A Grammy in February, a self-titled debut in March, and a year of people arguing about what to call her, which she mostly ignored.

years.src: Grammy.com: Tyla wins Best African Music Performance · Wikipedia: Tyla (singer)
yt: Tyla wins Best African Music Performance
years.h: Tyla wins the first Best African Music Performance Grammy
years.p: "Water" beat a field that, per Grammy.com, was four Nigerian or Nigerian-descended entries out of five, including [[Burna Boy|78a19169-ac75-4868-b504-7e2e073118e0]] and [[Davido|a9ae7d4b-10f0-4da8-8b8c-21722a074a54]].
years.xp:
The category was new that year. Wikipedia calls her the youngest African artist to win a Grammy; Grammy.com notes she was 22 and that the dance challenge had passed 1.5 million videos.

The Recording Academy describes the category as music with a stylistic intention or representation found in Africa and the diaspora.

q: a lithe, contemporary take on pop-R&B that pulses with the log-drum heartbeat of amapiano
years.src: Wikipedia: Tyla (album) · Album of the Year: Tyla reviews · OkayAfrica: Sammy Soso interview · Wikipedia: Art (song) · Pop Crave on X: Tyla 22nd best album of 2024
years.p: Pitchfork gave the FAX/Epic debut an 8.0 and later ranked it No. 22 on its best albums of 2024, calling it a pop-R&B record driven by amapiano's log drum.
years.xp:
[[Sammy Soso|44c1e43c-24d4-4995-9d68-acfa0cb14f13]] produced 10 of the 14 tracks, and told OkayAfrica they recorded around 130 songs for it, with about 30 percussion channels stacked on "Safer". Guests are [[Kelvin Momo|c5726285-7b7c-43ce-b107-dae084cf5e6c]] on the intro, [[Tems|5b2a8faa-ffee-4706-a1a8-58f109bc8ca2]] on "No.1", [[Gunna|100b8734-f4f0-4536-9960-47f7c59d1b4c]] and [[Skillibeng|2f639ba8-11ee-4128-9915-2303afd30078]] on "Jump", [[Becky G|eb90c8b8-d733-4c14-a293-105c3d1ba9b3]] on "On My Body" and Travis Scott on the "Water" remix. "Art" followed on April 12 with a Nabil Elderkin video set in a gallery, and Tyla played it on Colbert that month.

Wikipedia lists a Metacritic score of 84 and a No. 24 Billboard 200 debut, the highest for a female African soloist. Year-end, Album of the Year tallies Rolling Stone No. 6, Billboard No. 13 and NME No. 19. The Line of Best Fit gave it 9/10.

years.src: Complex: Tyla on identifying as Black and Coloured · Wikipedia: Tyla (singer)
years.h: The Breakfast Club asks about "Coloured", and she answers on X
years.p: After Charlamagne tha God questioned her identity on air, Tyla wrote that she never denied her Blackness and is "both Coloured in South Africa and a Black [woman]".
years.xp: Complex traces the argument to a 2020 TikTok where she called herself a Coloured South African. She has explained she has Zulu, Irish, Mauritian and Indian ancestry, and noted the word reads differently in America than at home.

years.h: Most BET Awards of the night, tied, and a stage with Gunna
years.p: Wikipedia says she tied [[Usher|3414d446-735a-443c-931f-10634f57e5b9]] and [[Victoria Monét|28d83274-26ab-4a6a-b9ff-340f4784e7dd]] for the most wins at the 2024 BET Awards, and performed "Jump" live in Los Angeles.

years.h: Tyla+ adds "Push 2 Start", then three MTV EMAs
years.p: The deluxe edition's reggae-tinged new single won her Best African Act, Best Afrobeats Artist and Best R&B Artist at the November 11 MTV Europe Music Awards.

eras.title: Grown up, still partying
eras.text: She's hosting Nickelodeon, selling out Tokyo, lending hooks to Cardi B and Zara Larsson, and announcing a second album at the Grammys.

years.p: Wikipedia calls her the first African solo artist to reach a billion on Spotify with one song, a mark "Water" hit in February 2025.
years.xp: Later that spring she played Coachella and premiered "Bliss" (released May 9). WWP, a summer EP she called a bridge to her second album, arrived July 25.

years.h: "Chanel" becomes her biggest global hit since "Water"
years.p: The A-Pop lead single reached No. 11 on the Billboard Global 200 and No. 43 on the Hot 100, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: A-Pop was officially announced on February 1, 2026, during the Grammys, where she also won Best African Music Performance a second time for "Push 2 Start", a first in the category.

years.h: Opening the World Cup with Future
years.p: Tyla performed "Game Time" with [[Future|48262e82-db9f-4a92-b650-dfef979b73ec]] at the 2026 FIFA World Cup opening ceremony in the U.S., and sang South Africa's anthem before its match with Mexico.
